title: Saints signing ex-Raider Daniel Carlson to bolster kicking competition: Source
content:
The New Orleans Saints are adding to their training camp kicker competition by signing All-Pro kicker Daniel Carlson, a league source who spoke on condition of anonymity because they don’t have permission to comment publicly, confirmed to The Athletic.

Carlson, 31, was released by the Las Vegas Raiders in March after spending the previous eight seasons as the franchise’s kicker. After leading the NFL in scoring in 2020, Carlson earned second-team All-Pro honors in 2021, followed by first-team All-Pro honors in 2022. He’s coming off a season in which he converted 81.5 percent of his kicks for the Raiders, his lowest season percentage since his second year in the NFL in 2019.

Three of the five kicks Carlson missed last season were from more than 50 yards. However, the timelines of some of his misses put a brighter spotlight on his struggles. In Week 9, Carlson missed a 48-yard field goal with less than five minutes left in regulation that would have tied the game. The Broncos got the ball back and ran out the clock for a 10-7 victory. The following week, Carlson had his lone missed extra point of the season in a 30-29 overtime loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Throughout the season, Carlson also had to navigate a bad offense overall in Las Vegas, which led him to attempt just 27 kicks, his lowest since 2019.

Despite Carlson coming off a down season for himself, he does offer a boost to the kicking situation in New Orleans. The Saints began last season with Blake Grupe as their kicker. Through the first 12 weeks of the season, Grupe led the league in missed field goals with eight, and the Saints had the second-worst field goal percentage among teams at 69.2 percent. After missing two kicks — from 38 yards and 47 yards — against the Atlanta Falcons, the Saints released Grupe and elevated Charlie Smyth from the practice squad.

Smyth has been in a competition with Tanner Brown, whom the Saints signed in June, throughout training camp. Smyth missed a 52-yard field goal in the team’s preseason opener while Brown made field goals from 49 and 29 yards. However, in the team’s second preseason game on Saturday, Brown missed the team’s lone field-goal attempt from 39 yards out.

Carlson’s signing puts both Smyth and Brown in the hot seat, but especially Brown. With roster cutdown day less than a week away, if Carlson wins the job, Smyth could get a spot on the team’s practice squad again without counting toward the 16-player practice squad limit because Smyth still falls under the NFL’s International Player Pathway Program.
